152741.overview: Croaka-Crawla is a clone of the arcade game Frogger where the player must control a frog and get him to the other side of a road and river. The game is viewed from above and the first thing to cross is a busy road full of traffic scrolling across the screen. You can move left, right or forward as you dodge the traffic to reach a river bank. Once the road has been survived then a river must be crossed by jumping on logs or the backs of turtles that scroll across the screen as well. Once you reach the other side of the river you must jump into a gap and occasionally a baby frog or flies appears for extra points. If you get hit by a vehicle, fall into the river, or touch the sides of the screen then you lose one of three lives. Before the game you can change the speed of the game (1-100) with 1 being the fastest.

152742.overview: City Patrol: In this 1st person shooter, you are in command of a Laser-Cannon Platform and you must defend your city from alien invaders attempting to destroy it. Controlling your sights, you must move about the city, scrolling left or right, in search of the invaders. Once you find one you must blast it before any damage is inflicted to the buildings or yourself. As you fire you must be careful as you can also destroy buildings as well. Your Laser-cannon can take five hits before it is destroyed and it is game over. Before the game you can choose a skill level from moderate, difficult or impossible.

152875.overview:
Centipede is an early attempt to bring Atari's arcade game with the same name to a home computer. The player controls a laser base at the bottom of the screen and has to shoot at the centipede-like aliens that appear at the top of the screen and then crawls towards him. Unlike the Atari game, the player can only move left and right and not up and down. Neither does it feature any mushrooms. Instead, there are only a few obstacles that stop the centipedes and make them change direction. When a centipede is shot, it splits into two halves. The player must shoot all segments before they reach the baseline. If they do, the player loses a base. The number of bases is user defined (1 to 5) and so is the movement speed of the centipedes. Another feature not present in the arcade game is that the centipedes can drop bombs at the player.

It's historically significant as this was Jeff Minter's very first commercial release.

152876.overview:
Take control of a football team in a division below the top one, and try to lead them to glory in both league and European competition. You start with a squad of 12 players, whose names can be changed, but have room for 15 players in total, with chances to buy and sell players. You can take out a bank loan, the level of which depends on your division.

The team's formation can be customised, and as outfield players are not limited to a single position, you can customise the team's strengths and weaknesses in quite a precise way. Matches are played out by listing scorers as they happen, and are followed by a full list of the division's other results. Finances change after each match to to wages, gate receipts, and possible incidents such as riots and illegal player approaches.

152890.overview: The classic game of chess against the computer. The AI has six skill levels and can effectively play both sides as the player can ask for recommendations which are calculated according to current level. Moves are performed by typing in the coordinates and the game supports advanced moves like castling.

188090.overview: Cosmic Guerilla is an unofficial conversion of Universal's arcade game with the same name. The basic gameplay is mostly the same although the scenario differs a bit. Here, the cosmic guerillas are raiding a city in space which the player has to defend. At his disposal he has his Svlegian Raider which is moved across the bottom of the screen while shooting at the enemies above. The enemies begin at the sides of the screen and move towards the centre where supply pods are located. The pods are protected by barriers that the aliens will remove one piece at a time. Once they have made a whole through they can take the pods and transport them back to the edge of the screen. The player has to prevent them from doing this by shooting them down in time. At the same time he has to watch out for their fire. Some protection is offered by four Space Invaders-esque shields. The player has three lives and loses one when shot or when the aliens recover a pod. Before a game, one of three game speeds can be chosen.

423939.overview:
Can of Worms is a collection of eight small aand humorous games:

Acne: You are Dr. Frankenstein and you have brought your monster alive, but problem is, his face is breaking out in acne. You must move a cursor around the monster's face and remove as much acne as you can.

Vasectomy: You are a surgeon and your latest surgery is a vasectomy but you are drunk and the patients 'manhood' seems to be moving around all over the place. You have to move a pair of scissors around the screen to catch the moving organ and snip it in the right place.

Smut: A program that shows four random words on screen attempting to show a smutty sentence.

Hitler: Hitler is alive in an old people's home in Cambridge and moves about in a wheelchair. You have been given the task to kill him by giving him a heart attack. To do this you must place a whoopee cushion underneath him by picking a number on where you think he will stop. You have to successfully place the cushion ten times to kill him.

Dole: You are in Government and you you are presented with five items and their figures which are Cuts, Inflation, Majority, Dole and Term. You must survive for as long as possible by adjusting the figures to keep everyone happy and not get the sack.

Royal Flush: The King is on the toilet but the pipes are prone to suffer blockages. It is your job to remove the offending blockage by choosing a number between one and nine and then flushing. Too little flush and the blockage stays, too much and the King gets covered.

Reagan: Plays like Acne but instead of removing spots you have have to remove grey hair from the head of former President of the USA, Ronald Reagan.

P's 'n' Q's: You want to pee but the toilet appears in various places and you have to make sure your stream hits the bowl. You choose a number between one and ten to choose the power of your peeing.
